parts.lead:
Four-camera inertial module from Shenzhen Tujian Intelligent Technology (图间智能). Four global-shutter RGB cameras sit on separate 25 × 25 mm boards, cabled to one controller with a Bosch BMI088 IMU; two cameras have 160° lenses and two have 200° lenses, and the baseline is set by how the boards are mounted. One recording, solved as four cameras + IMU.

4 camerasGlobal shutter200° fisheye200 Hz IMU
parts.glance:
Four-camera inertial module from Shenzhen Tujian Intelligent Technology (图间智能). Four global-shutter RGB cameras sit on separate 25 × 25 mm boards, cabled to one controller with a Bosch BMI088 IMU; two cameras have 160° lenses and two have 200° lenses, and the baseline is set by how the boards are mounted. One recording, solved as four cameras + IMU.

Reprojection median0.19 px
cam0–cam1 baseline66.6 mm
cam0 td+0.80 ms
cam0 lever arm59.7 mm

Reprojection is how far, in pixels, the detected corners lie from where the solve puts them. td is the camera–IMU time offset, and the lever arm is the camera–IMU position offset.

No independent reference, so these values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.

parts.limits:
• No independent reference, so these values show what MVIS solved, not how close they are to the truth.
  • The board never reached the outer side of the two 200° images (about two-thirds of each image is covered), so the lens model there is extrapolated.
  • The IMU noise set for the solve is wider than the residuals need (IMU χ²/dof 0.03); a solve with tighter noise is still to do.
  • The tag size is taken from the target file sent with the data and isn't confirmed on the printed board. It scales every baseline and lever arm.
parts.run: • All four cameras and the IMU together. Camera intrinsics (Kannala–Brandt kb4) from four single-camera solves of the same recording, then held fixed; IMU scale and misalignment, gyro-to-accel offset t_ga and camera time offsets estimated. IMU noise from the BMI088 datasheet, about 2.5× wider. Solved 2026-11-11.

Lens Calibrated field of view

Calibrated field of view, horizontal × vertical. cam0: 131° × 110°, corners reach 77° from the axis · cam1: 131° × 110°, corners reach 77° from the axis · cam2: 170° × 137°, corners reach 86° from the axis · cam3: ~171° × 137°, corners reach 87° from the axis

cam0 cam1 cam2 cam3

We read these from the calibrated lens fit at the image edges, through the principal point (where the optical axis meets the image). ~ marks an axis past where the corners reached, so the fit is extrapolated there. Past the fit means an edge lies beyond where the fit holds, so we give no value.
